newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe, Malawi discuss increasing trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe, Malawi discuss increasing trade.

text.p: Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe met Malawi's President Bakili Muluzi on Friday for talks on bilateral and regional issues that concentrated on trade, senior government officials said.
Zimbabwean and Malawian Foreign Ministers Stan Mudenge and George Mutafu told reporters the leaders' discussions covered mainly prospects for increasing trade and economic cooperation.
"We want to expand in areas of tourism, improve transport modalities, cross-border investment, and cooperation in the field of agriculture where Zimbabwe is a leading producer," Mutafu said.
Annual trade between the two southern African states is estimated at about Z$320 million ($32 million), with the balance in favour of Zimbabwe at about Z$250 million ($25 million).
Zimbabwe imports cereals, mainly rice, fertiliser, assembled buses and steel from Malawi while its exports include paperboard, tobacco, sugar and alcoholic beverages.
Muluzi arrived in Harare on Thursday to officially open Zimbabwe's annual agricultural show on Friday.
